about: The library page, as one noun: a catalog of the seed-pack library at one pinned commit, copied from the library's own nouns. scripts/sync_library.py writes the measured part (the source's commit, committed_at and tessera_commit, the totals and every pack) from a clean checkout of the library at that commit, and keeps the rest exactly as written: the words, the categories, their intros and which category holds each pack. The library's manifests carry no category, so the categories are this noun's own explicit mapping, made by reading each pack. scripts/build_site.py checks the noun and renders it into site/library/index.html; it never fetches anything. Every pack is a proposal: nothing here is installed, admitted or running.
title: Library | ta-amps
description: Every seed pack in the ta-amps library, grouped by what it is for, with its nouns and verbs counted at one pinned commit. Every pack is a proposal checked offline with Tessera's models; importing a pack runs nothing.
heading: Library
lead: Every seed pack in the library, grouped by what it is for. A pack is a collection of task objects (nouns), the reusable things, and durable tasks (things to do), the work an authorized worker can claim on Tessera’s shared durable task queue.
dateline: Every pack is a proposal checked offline with Tessera's models; importing or reading a pack runs nothing.

source.read: packs/<pack>/manifest.json, nouns.json and verbs.json, packs/VALIDATION.json and .github/workflows/, at the commit above

words.counted: Counted from the library at commit
words.checked: Every noun and verb was checked offline with Tessera’s own models.
words.badge_note: The pack ships its own code with tests, which the library’s CI runs for that pack.

categories.name: Nonprofit agent kits and public-solution packs
categories.intro: Agent kits that a nonprofit’s own agent runs on its files. The agent drafts, and it never decides about a person or contacts anyone. Also here: how to build a new kit, and two packs that answer from official public sources, citing every point.

categories.name: Video, voice and media
categories.intro: Making a video with code, from script to release: scenes, motion, an AI voice labeled as AI, captions, editing, checks, review, cut-downs, thumbnails and an audience test. A person approves what is published.

categories.name: Research and analysis
categories.intro: Questions answered from evidence: cited research reports, public companies and options chains described but never as financial advice, checked CSV analysis, repository reviews, measured cost savings, and example cases screened for exploitation without accusing anyone.

categories.name: Quality, testing and accessibility
categories.intro: Checking work the way its users would: an accessibility audit against WCAG 2.2 AA, acceptance tests with criteria agreed first, usability and design reviews, exploratory sessions, a launch check, a local-only security review and clearer docs. Every sign-off and go decision stays with a person.

categories.name: Engineering workflow
categories.intro: Work that comes back in every project: direction turned into atomic durable tasks, big jobs split into steps, unattended runs that leave a record, status with evidence, findings fixed and verified, releases and renames, reuse before rebuilding, file triage and claims that say how they are known.

categories.name: Learning and evaluation
categories.intro: Measuring before trusting: a small open model tuned round after round and kept only when a rule fixed in advance says so, fair evaluations with pass marks set first, checks proven on good and bad examples, current benchmark scores and a person’s recorded choices.

categories.name: Architecture and discovery
categories.intro: Finding what exists before building, then fitting the pieces together: new tools and repositories trialed, prior art surveyed, stale knowledge flagged, tested code composed without rewriting it, and any agent harness connected and proven end to end.
